policy.PASSED: Only if evidence[] is non-empty AND every listed test/control is green in CI
policy.NOT_VERIFIED: Default when no real evidence mapped — NEVER treat as PASSED
policy.FAILED: Mapped evidence exists and at least one failed
policy.N/A: Category does not apply to this project — requires Ω justification in notes
policy.certificateComplete: All categories are PASSED or N/A (justified) — zero NOT_VERIFIED, zero FAILED

A01.name: Broken Access Control
controls: Deny by default
Object-level authorization (no ID-only fetch without ownership/tenant scope)
Function-level authorization on privileged actions
CORS / force browsing hardened
A01.notes: Verified via RBAC middleware tests and CORS fail-closed policy.

A02.name: Cryptographic Failures
controls: TLS in transit for sensitive data
No secrets in source control
Strong algorithms / key management by Ω
Sensitive data classified and minimized
A02.notes: Bcrypt password hashing, HS512 JWT signatures, and Stripe HMAC-SHA256 verification verified.

A03.name: Injection
controls: Parameterized queries / no raw string SQL with user input
Output encoding for XSS surfaces
Command injection avoided (no shell with untrusted input)
Schema validation on inputs (e.g. Zod / pydantic)
A03.notes: 100% parameterized SQL queries via MariaDB pool.execute and Zod schema validation.

A04.name: Insecure Design
controls: Threat model or security notes in FC for product features
Business logic abuse considered in Gherkin
Least privilege by design
Rate limits / anti-automation where applicable
A04.notes: 2FA email verification flow and rate limiting on sensitive endpoints.

A05.name: Security Misconfiguration
controls: Hardened defaults (no debug in prod)
Security headers where web (CSP, HSTS, etc. as stack allows)
Unnecessary features disabled
Environment separation (local ≠ prod URLs in tests)
A05.notes: Helmet headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) and fail-closed CORS.

A06.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
controls: Dependency audit (npm/bun audit, pip-audit, govulncheck, etc.)
Pinned versions for production builds
Process to patch critical CVEs
Remove unused dependencies
A06.notes: Automated dependency vulnerability audit script verifying 0 high/critical vulnerabilities.

A07.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
controls: Secure session / token handling
Password / MFA policy as product requires
No default credentials
Brute-force / lockout or rate limit on auth endpoints
A07.notes: HttpOnly cookie sessions and authRateLimiter 5 req/15 min lockout protection.

A08.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
controls: CI integrity (no unsigned deploy of product without process)
Integrity of updates / artifacts
Deserialize untrusted data carefully
Signed FC + tests same commit for product code
A08.notes: Protocol L CI integrity gate (verifyL) and Zod schema validation.

A09.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
controls: Auth and access-control failures logged
No secrets in logs
Alert path defined for critical security events
Forensic trail (F / audit log) for security-relevant product changes
A09.notes: Sanitized SHA-256 payload audit logging without plaintext secrets.

A10.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
controls: Validate/allowlist outbound URLs from user input
Block link-local / metadata IPs where relevant
Network egress policy for services
No blind proxy of user-supplied URLs
A10.notes: Origin validation on external webhooks and zero proxying of arbitrary user-supplied URLs.
